title: The Emancipation Proclamation
objective: After this level you can explain what the 1863 Proclamation did and did not do, and why Lincoln issued it as a war measure.
summary: Lincoln issued the Emancipation Proclamation as a war measure. From January 1, 1863, it freed enslaved people in rebelling areas, spared loyal ones, and opened the Army to Black men.

cards.headline: Lincoln’s most famous order skipped every slave state loyal to the Union.
cards.body: The Emancipation Proclamation declared people free only where the rebellion ruled. Why write it that way, and what did it still change?

cards.headline: Save the Union first
cards.body: In August 1862, Horace Greeley, a New York editor, pressed Lincoln to free the enslaved. Lincoln answered in public: “My paramount object in this struggle is to save the Union.” What he didn’t say was that a draft of an emancipation proclamation was already on his desk. The public letter told only half the story.

cards.headline: A war measure
cards.body: The moment came after the Union victory at Antietam. On September 22, 1862, Lincoln issued a preliminary proclamation, and the final one took effect on January 1, 1863. He acted as commander in chief, calling it “a fit and necessary war measure for suppressing said rebellion.” Framed that way, freedom became a weapon against the Confederacy.

cards.headline: What it did, and didn’t
cards.body: It declared that enslaved people in areas in rebellion “are, and henceforward shall be free.” It left slavery untouched in the loyal border states and in Confederate areas the Union already held. But every advance of Union troops after that day widened the area of freedom. And it announced that Black men would be accepted into the Union Army and Navy. Freedom now marched with the army.

cards.headline: The Emancipation Proclamation: explained
learned: Lincoln put saving the Union first, but had a draft ready
Issued after Antietam as a war measure, effective January 1, 1863
It freed people in rebel areas, not in loyal border states
It opened the Union Army and Navy to Black men

questions.prompt: Where did the Emancipation Proclamation leave slavery untouched?

options.label: In every state of the Confederacy
options.rationale: Those were the areas it was aimed at.

options.label: In the loyal border states and Union-held Confederate areas
Only in Texas, the westernmost Confederate state
options.rationale: Texas was in rebellion, so it was covered.

options.label: In areas still in rebellion
options.rationale: Rebel areas were exactly where it declared freedom.

questions.explanation: It applied only to areas in rebellion, sparing the loyal border states and Union-held areas.

questions.prompt: Why did Lincoln issue emancipation as a war measure?

options.label: Congress had already abolished slavery everywhere
options.rationale: Slavery was still legal in loyal states.

options.label: The Supreme Court had ordered him to act
He acted as commander in chief to weaken the rebellion
Greeley’s newspaper had the power to require it
options.rationale: A newspaper can argue, not command.

questions.explanation: As commander in chief, he called it “a fit and necessary war measure for suppressing said rebellion.”

questions.prompt: Lincoln feared pushing loyal slave states toward the Confederacy. How does the Proclamation show that fear?

options.label: It exempted the loyal border states
It freed people in Kentucky first
options.rationale: Kentucky was loyal, so it was exempt.

options.label: It barred Black men from the Army
options.rationale: It opened the Army to Black men.

options.label: It was issued before the war began
options.rationale: It came in the war’s third year.

questions.explanation: It left slavery untouched in the loyal border states Lincoln was trying to keep.
